\section{Round-eight reconstruction: renormalized birth bundle, UNI, and the correctly scaled vector--roof LLT}
\label{sec:r8-a2}

We distinguish three logically different ingredients: the physical quotient
through orbit births, compact-frequency aperiodicity, and high-frequency
nonlocal integrability.  The local limit statement is written in sum variables
first and then translated to windows for the normalized roof average.

\subsection{The renormalized physical current bundle}

Let $E_R:\mathbb B\to\mathscr D'$ be the realization of the ambient trace
coordinates.  At a simple birth $R_0$ choose a smooth ambient splitting
$\mathbb B=B^{\rm old}\oplus B^{\rm b}$ for which
\[
 E_R(x,y)=E_R^{\rm old}x+(R-R_0)\widetilde E_R^{\rm b}y.
\]
Define the fiber norm
\[
 \|(x,y)\|_{\mathbb B_R^\sharp}
 =\|x\|+|R-R_0|\|y\|
\]
after quotienting $\ker E_R$.  The physical range is given its inherited
anisotropic distribution norm, not a tautological quotient norm.

\begin{lemma}[Uniform birth chart]
\label{lem:r8-a2-birth}
If $E_{R_0}^{\rm old}$ and $\widetilde E_{R_0}^{\rm b}$ have transverse closed
ranges, then, after shrinking the parameter chart, the induced realization
\[
 \overline E_R:\mathbb B_R^\sharp/\ker E_R\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ran}E_R
\]
is an isomorphism with uniformly bounded norm and inverse norm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Rescale the birth coordinate by $z=(R-R_0)y$.  In $(x,z)$ coordinates the
realization is $E_R^{\rm old}x+\widetilde E_R^{\rm b}z$, a continuous
perturbation of a bounded-below operator on the transverse sum at $R_0$.
The bounded inverse theorem is uniform on a smaller compact chart.  Pulling the
norm back gives exactly $\|x\|+|R-R_0|\|y\|$.  No inverse of an order-one
ambient birth coordinate is claimed at the point where its physical current
vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Continuous physical quotient field]
\label{thm:r8-a2-field}
The old, birth, death, face, and corner charts glue to a Hausdorff continuous
field $\{\mathscr B_R^{\rm phys}\}_{R\in K}$.  The billiard transfer operators
and their first $m$ parameter derivatives act on one fixed strong/weak scale
of this field and satisfy uniform Lasota--Yorke estimates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On overlaps, both charts are identified through their common physical current.
Lemma~\ref{lem:r8-a2-birth} makes the transition maps uniformly bounded.  A
death chart is the reversed birth chart.  Trace jets are triangular by
codimension, and each moving-boundary derivative lowers one strong order.  The
usual branch estimate is therefore uniform after the renormalized coordinate
is used.  Compactness follows from finite chart cover, cylinder truncation,
and one-order loss.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Periodic separation and a finite family of certificates}

Let
\[
 c_R(v)=\bigl(S_v\kappa_R^{(1)},S_v\kappa_R^{(2)},S_v\tau_R,|v|\bigr)
 \in\mathbb R^4
\]
for a periodic inducing word $v$.

\begin{lemma}[Periodic span algorithm]
\label{lem:r8-a2-span}
Suppose no nonzero affine combination of
$\kappa_R^{(1)},\kappa_R^{(2)},\tau_R,1$ is a coboundary on the physical
quotient.  Then periodic vectors affinely span $\mathbb R^4$.  Enumerating
admissible primitive words therefore terminates with five words
$v_0,\ldots,v_4$ whose difference determinant is nonzero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If the affine span were proper, a nonzero affine functional would be constant
on every periodic sum.  Apply the cylinder cohomology construction: define a
transfer value along a word by subtracting that constant and use equality on
all periodic loops to make it path independent.  This produces a continuous
coboundary, contradicting the hypothesis.  Linear algebra then selects five
periodic vectors.  Enumeration terminates because a nonzero determinant is a
finite certificate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Finite parameter-uniform certificate family]
\label{thm:r8-a2-certificates}
There are finitely many five-word packets $\mathcal W_1,\ldots,\mathcal W_M$
and open parameter sets $K_\alpha$ covering $K$ such that
\[
 |\det D_{R,\alpha}|\ge d_\alpha>0,
 \qquad R\in K_\alpha.
\]
The Fourier proof chooses a packet according to the parameter chart; it does
not concatenate packets into one fictitious global determinant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{lem:r8-a2-span} gives one packet at each $R$.  Periodic collision
coordinates and sums vary continuously while the word remains admissible, so
its determinant stays nonzero on a neighborhood.  Compactness of $K$ gives a
finite subcover.  A subordinate partition in parameter space selects the
corresponding estimate without altering any orbit word.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A separate geometric UNI theorem}

For inverse branches $h,k$ of a common return iterate define the temporal
distance
\[
 \Delta_{h,k}(x)=\tau_n(hx)-\tau_n(kx).
\]

\begin{lemma}[Dispersing two-branch derivative]
\label{lem:r8-a2-uni-geometry}
On each compact finite-horizon geometry chart there exist two admissible
returned branches $h,k$, an unstable interval $J$, and $c_{\rm uni}>0$ such
that
\[
 |\partial_x\Delta_{h,k}(x)|\ge c_{\rm uni},\qquad x\in J.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose two itineraries agreeing up to one collision and leaving that scatterer
through two distinct strictly convex arcs before returning to the same base.
For a free flight from $r(x)$ to $r'(x)$,
\[
 \partial_x\tau=\widehat{r'-r}\cdot(\partial_xr'-\partial_xr).
\]
Subtracting the two itineraries cancels the common legs.  Strict convexity and
the non-tangency of the two outgoing directions make the remaining derivative
nonzero at the reference orbit.  Uniform curvature, finite horizon, and a
compact chart shrink $J$ so that the lower bound is uniform.  Markov
specification supplies common return connectors; they contribute identical
terminal legs and do not change the derivative difference.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[High-frequency Dolgopyat contraction]
\label{thm:r8-a2-dolgopyat}
For the twisted physical transfer operator
$\mathcal L_{R,\xi,b}$, where $\xi$ is the two-dimensional homology frequency
and $b$ the roof frequency, there are $C,\gamma>0$ such that
\[
 \|\mathcal L_{R,\xi,b}^{n(b)}\|_{\rm phys}
 \le 1-C|b|^{-\gamma}
\]
for $|b|$ large and $\xi$ in a fixed fundamental domain.  Face and corner
currents satisfy the same estimate on the renormalized field.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{lem:r8-a2-uni-geometry} gives an interval on which
$b\Delta_{h,k}$ crosses a fixed phase interval.  Split the interval into
near-opposition pieces and their complement.  On a near-opposition piece,
\[
 |zu+wv|\le(|z|+|w|)(1-c\alpha^2)
\]
when the phase error is at most $\alpha$ and the two amplitudes are comparable.
Bounded distortion and cone invariance preserve comparability.  Nonconcentration
of unstable conditional measures supplies a definite mass of such pieces.
The remaining branches are controlled by Lasota--Yorke contraction.  Trace
jets form a finite triangular extension in each chart; the depth weights and
Lemma~\ref{lem:r8-a2-birth} absorb their off-diagonal terms.
\end{proof}

The finite-family periodic theorem is used only to exclude exact compact
frequency eigenfunctions.  The derivative theorem above supplies the distinct
large-frequency mechanism.

\subsection{The master vector--roof local limit formula}

Let $S_n\in\mathbb Z^2$ and $T_n\in\mathbb R$ be the homology sum and roof sum,
centered at their exact finite saddle.  Write $\Sigma_R$ for the nonsingular
three-dimensional covariance and let $\varphi_{\Sigma_R}$ be its Gaussian
density.

\begin{theorem}[Correctly scaled vector--roof LLT]
\label{thm:r8-a2-llt}
Uniformly for lattice targets $k_n$ in a bounded central range and bounded
Borel sets $B\subset\mathbb R$ with negligible boundary,
\[
 \mathbb P_R\!\left(
 S_n=k_n,\ \frac{T_n}{n}\in t_n+G_nB
 \right)
 =\frac{1}{n}\int_{\sqrt n(t_n-\bar\tau_R)+\sqrt n G_nB}
 \varphi_{\Sigma_R}\!\left(
 \frac{k_n-n\bar\kappa_R}{\sqrt n},u
 \right)du+o(n^{-1})
\]
whenever $G_n\to0$; the same formula with the corresponding Gaussian interval
holds for fixed $G_n$.  In particular, if $\sqrt nG_n\to0$, the leading order
is $G_n n^{-1/2}$, not $G_n n^{-3/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fourier inversion gives a joint two-lattice/one-continuous density of order
$n^{-3/2}$ in the roof-sum variable.  The average window
$T_n/n\in t_n+G_nB$ is a roof-sum interval of length $nG_n$.  Changing variables
$u=(T_n-nt_n)/\sqrt n$ contributes the factor $\sqrt n$, yielding the displayed
$n^{-1}$ Gaussian integral.  Compact frequencies use
Theorem~\ref{thm:r8-a2-certificates}; large roof frequencies use
Theorem~\ref{thm:r8-a2-dolgopyat}; the remaining minor arcs are exponentially
small by the physical spectral gap.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Three unambiguous regimes]
\label{cor:r8-a2-regimes}
If $G_n\ll n^{-1/2}$, the coefficient is the local-density expression
$G_n n^{-1/2}$.  If $G_n\asymp n^{-1/2}$, it is $n^{-1}$ times a finite Gaussian
interval mass.  If $n^{-1/2}\ll G_n\le G_0$, it is $n^{-1}$ times the saturated
conditional Gaussian mass.  One target-dependent saddle is used in all three
regimes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply dominated convergence to the Gaussian integral in
Theorem~\ref{thm:r8-a2-llt} in the three ranges of $\sqrt nG_n$.
\end{proof}
